Triggers

What starts work on its own: [triggers] (what libraos-engine trigger status prints, and templates for it), and beside it [improve] and [signals]. All three are off by default, only an owner sees this page, and nothing here turns any of them on: that is a terminal step.

← Overview

A session is an agent connected to this host. A handoff records a task, its context, and who has taken it. A worker is a session started for a handoff. Tasks brings the work together, and its Needs me holds decisions and updates that need you; the Agents list beside the rail shows what needs you and what is running.

Where things are

Overview
Where the server opens: how loaded the server, its tasks and its agents are, every task running now, and what needs a person.
Tasks
The board of work, and the New handoff form when dispatch is on. Needs me (the Inbox) is there too: approvals, blocked and failed workers waiting on you.
Team
Users (an owner invites, resets and disables them there), Permissions (who has which role where; an owner or admin changes them with their password), Nodes and devices, and Activity.
Insights
Success, Cost, Usage, Metrics, History and Worker usage as tabs, with the period and Whose work under them; each says what it covers.
Chat
Conversations with a role.
Settings
Server (agents, models, workers, connections, repositories, roles, sessions on this host and Triggers), Access, and your Personal settings.

Words used here

Unassigned
A task offered for an agent to take.
Working
The host process reports activity; a session can be connected without doing work.
Not seen
The session has not checked in recently. This is separate from the task’s result.
Reserved resource
A path or port an agent says it is using, recorded as a claim.
Validation
A check of the work. A passing check does not merge or publish it.
Lower bound (≥)
At least this amount is known; some usage or prices are missing.
From / Taken by
The session that offered the task and the session that claimed it.

From the command line

Every command takes -h. Start with libraos-engine doctor to see whether this install works, and libraos-engine status for what is waiting.
